xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-4833: Phone app: packages/anywhere-channel, one channel protocol for server and phone

plan.title: Phone app: packages/anywhere-channel, one channel protocol for server and phone
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

metadata.sizeJustification: One new workspace package plus the import sites of two protocol files that must move in one commit to keep the server building. The projected-surface lint counts each root file (package.json, bun.lock) and each top-level directory pair as a subsystem; the real change is the package, its server importers in src/lib/anywhere/channel and src/dashboard/server, and two docs. The issue is already one work item (W-WEB1) split from epic PAN-4823; its browser pieces are each a separate item here and share the package's crypto port and initiator.

narratives.Problem: The phone app (epic PAN-4823) must speak the secure channel byte for byte, but noise.ts and wire.ts use node:crypto and Buffer and live in the server tree, and the browser has no RTCDataChannel duplex, no directory client and no machine dialer. Whether pure-JS libsodium is fast enough in a phone WebView is unproven (CP-1).
narratives.Proposal: Create the private MIT workspace package @overdeck/anywhere-channel with entries '.', './node' and './web'. Pin golden vectors on current code, move noise.ts and wire.ts into the package behind an explicit CryptoPort (Node and web implementations), extract the initiator handshake into a shared runInitiatorHandshake with a same-tick finisher used by the server's openChannel and the phone's openSecureChannel, add RtcDuplexWeb, DirectoryWebClient and createMachineDialer, prove web-to-Node handshakes with a cross-port test, and measure CP-1 in throttled Chromium, WebKit and the Android emulator. Details: .pan/drafts/PAN-4833.md.
narratives.NonGoals:
- HTTP/1.1 and WebSocket clients over the channel, the pool and the fetch/WebSocket page shims (PAN-4834)
- The Capacitor app, key storage, sign-in and pairing UI (PAN-4837), and the iOS Simulator CP-1 leg
- The directory's client role and subprotocol auth on /v1/directory (PAN-4829) and the client-role contract types (PAN-4828)
- Moving accept.ts, channel-socket.ts, channel-agent.ts, rtc-transport.ts, rtc-duplex.ts or relay-ice-servers.ts out of src/lib/anywhere/channel/
- Approval mode on the web
- Any change to wire bytes, NOISE_LINK_PROTOCOL (stays 1), CONNECT_PROTOCOL_VERSION or the server responder's behavior
- Publishing @overdeck/anywhere-channel to npm
- Correcting pan-2350 D-2 (pan-4823 W-DOC)
- Raising any row in scripts/file-size-allowlist.txt

autoDecisions.summary: Extract the transport-agnostic initiator handshake from open.ts into packages/anywhere-channel/src/initiator.ts (PRD D-6), keeping open.ts on the server for transports and re-exporting the moved names.
autoDecisions.rationale: pan-4823 NFR-1 requires the phone and server to run the same protocol code; the phone needs exactly this sequence, and a second copy would drift. The issue says 'one channel protocol for server and phone'.

autoDecisions.summary: Keep two crypto ports (node:crypto and @noble/hashes + getRandomValues) as pan-4823 D-7 states, rather than a single sodium-universal implementation.
autoDecisions.rationale: D-7 names both ports and AC-5 tests them against each other; the port must work before libsodium loads.

autoDecisions.summary: Pass the CryptoPort as an explicit first argument (no module-global port).
autoDecisions.rationale: The cross-port test runs both ports in one process; a global would make that test meaningless.

autoDecisions.summary: dialMachine is a method of createMachineDialer(directory) and reuses one RTCPeerConnection per (machine, relay).
autoDecisions.rationale: The machine's RtcTransport.accept closes an older peer connection for the same key on every new offer, so a new connection per dial would kill the phone's pooled channels.

autoDecisions.summary: If PAN-4828's client-role contracts are not on main when directory-web starts, copy them verbatim into a temporary directory-frames.ts marked for deletion.
autoDecisions.rationale: Avoids stalling on a sibling issue without merging an unreviewed feature branch; the copy is mechanical and review can diff it.

autoDecisions.summary: CP-1 carries the secure channel over a WebSocket to a local Node responder; legs are throttled Chromium, WebKit and the galaxyA16 Android emulator; the iOS Simulator leg is deferred to PAN-4837.
autoDecisions.rationale: CP-1 measures libsodium-in-JS cost, not WebRTC; the iOS Simulator needs the Mac rig and the operator, and WebKit is the same engine.

autoDecisions.summary: @overdeck/anywhere-channel is private, source-exported (effect-acp pattern) and listed in root devDependencies.
autoDecisions.rationale: Both tsdown configs already bundle @overdeck/*; lint-dist-externals rejects workspace:* in published dependencies (PAN-3209).

narrative.Action: PRD WI-2, decisions D-1 and D-2. packages/anywhere-channel/package.json: name @overdeck/anywhere-channel, private true, type module, license MIT, exports '.'->./src/index.ts, './node'->./src/node.ts, './web'->./src/web.ts (types+import, effect-acp pattern, no build). dependencies exactly: noise-handshake 4.2.0, @hyperswarm/secret-stream 6.9.2, b4a 1.9.0, streamx 2.28.1, @noble/hashes 2.4.0, sodium-javascript 0.8.0, bare-events 2.9.2, @overdeck/contracts workspace:*; devDependencies vite ^8.3.1. tsconfig.json copies packages/contracts/tsconfig.json with lib [ES2022, DOM], types [node], noEmit true, include [src], and paths { '@overdeck/contracts': ['../contracts/src/index.ts'] } (frontend tsconfig pattern) so the package typecheck reads contracts source, not a stale dist. crypto-port.ts: interface CryptoPort { sha256(data: Uint8Array): Uint8Array; randomBytes(n: number): Uint8Array; timingSafeEqual(a: Uint8Array, b: Uint8Array): boolean }. crypto-node.ts: nodeCrypto wraps node:crypto createHash/randomBytes/timingSafeEqual (false on length mismatch). crypto-web.ts: webCrypto uses sha256 from '@noble/hashes/sha2.js', globalThis.crypto.getRandomValues in chunks of <=65536 bytes, constant-time compare with no early exit. index.ts exports type CryptoPort; node.ts exports nodeCrypto and re-exports index; web.ts exports webCrypto and re-exports index. Root package.json: add packages/anywhere-channel to workspaces.packages, add '@overdeck/anywhere-channel': 'workspace:*' to devDependencies (NOT dependencies: lint-dist-externals rejects workspace:* there), add script typecheck:anywhere-channel = 'tsc --noEmit -p packages/anywhere-channel/tsconfig.json' and append '&& npm run typecheck:anywhere-channel' to typecheck. src/dashboard/server/package.json: add the dependency next to @overdeck/contracts. Run bun install; commit bun.lock. No tsdown or vitest alias is needed.

metadata.parallelSafeReason: Depends only on move-protocol; it is the sole editor of open.ts and channel-socket.ts after that, and web-secure-channel waits on it.

narrative.Action: PRD WI-4, decision D-6. Move from open.ts into packages/anywhere-channel/src/initiator.ts, logic unchanged: ChannelOpenError, ChannelOpenErrorCode, ChannelOpenDetail, DEFAULT_OPEN_TIMEOUT_MS, the options union (as InitiatorOptions with localKey: StaticKeyPair), withDeadline, handshakeAsInitiator (as runInitiatorHandshake(raw, label, opts, crypto, track, finish)), readMessage, refusalToError, toOpenError; move ChannelMarker from channel-socket.ts. runInitiatorHandshake ends with: const leftover = reader.detach(); if (finalMessage) raw.write(encodeFrame(finalMessage)); return finish({ raw, handshake: handshake.result(), leftover, channel }); with no await between those statements (bytes behind the last frame are lost otherwise). Timers typed ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>; AbortController+setTimeout only. open.ts keeps TransportUrl, RtcDialer, setRtcDialer, FLY_INSTANCE_PARAM, parseTransportUrl, connectTransport, openChannel, openChannelOverTransport, now calling withDeadline + runInitiatorHandshake(raw, label, opts, nodeCrypto, track, done => createChannelSocket({ raw: done.raw, initiator: true, handshake: done.handshake, channel: done.channel, leftover: done.leftover })), and re-exports ChannelOpenError, type ChannelOpenErrorCode, type ChannelOpenDetail, DEFAULT_OPEN_TIMEOUT_MS, type OpenChannelOptions (alias of InitiatorOptions); channel-socket.ts re-exports type ChannelMarker. No importer of open.ts or channel-socket.ts changes its import specifier. initiator.test.ts imports only package code and builds the responder from xxPskResponder/ikResponder/encodeFrame/encodeRefusal over node:stream duplexPair(); timeout/abort cases use vi.useFakeTimers().

narrative.Action: PRD WI-6, decision D-7 (pan-4823 AC-5 first half). types/secret-stream.d.ts declares module '@hyperswarm/secret-stream' default class SecretStream extends streamx Duplex with constructor (isInitiator, rawStream, { handshake: { tx, rx, hash, publicKey, remotePublicKey: Uint8Array }, data?: Uint8Array }). secure-channel-web.ts (first line '/// <reference path="./types/secret-stream.d.ts" />'): openSecureChannel(raw: RawDuplex, opts: WebChannelOptions, label='machine'): Promise<SecureChannel> = withDeadline(label, opts, (_s, track) => { track(raw); return runInitiatorHandshake(raw, label, opts, webCrypto, track, d => ({ stream: new SecretStream(true, d.raw, { handshake: { tx: d.handshake.tx, rx: d.handshake.rx, hash: d.handshake.hash, publicKey: d.handshake.localPublicKey, remotePublicKey: d.handshake.remotePublicKey }, ...(d.leftover.length > 0 ? { data: d.leftover } : {}) }), channel: d.channel })); }). WebChannelOptions offers mode link (remoteKeyHex) and pairing (pairingCode) only, default timeout 10 s. web.ts exports openSecureChannel, type WebChannelOptions, type SecureChannel. Test: keys from createRequire(import.meta.url)('noise-handshake/dh').generateKeyPair(); server side is acceptChannel from src/lib/anywhere/channel/accept.ts on end A of node:stream duplexPair(); web side passes end B directly to openSecureChannel (a Node Duplex satisfies RawDuplex). Never import streamx, b4a or other package-only dependencies from tests/: they are not hoisted to the root node_modules.

items.title: Given a pairing code known to acceptChannel, when openSecureChannel runs in pairing mode, then both sides resolve, each side's channel.remoteKeyHex equals the other side's public key hex, and 64 KiB written in each direction arrives byte-identical

A link dial naming a key the responder does not hold rejects with ChannelOpenError code identity-refused, and a link dial whose key isPinnedPeer refuses rejects with code unknown-peer

Add DirectoryWebClient: the phone's directory socket with subprotocol auth, back-off and keepalive

narrative.Action: PRD WI-7, decisions D-9 and D-10. Precondition (D-9 checkpoint): git fetch origin main && git grep -q ClientToDirectoryFrame origin/main -- packages/contracts/src/connect.ts. If found, merge origin/main (pan sync-main pan-4833) and import ClientToDirectoryFrame, DirectoryToClientFrame, CONNECT_CLOSE_CODES, CONNECT_PROTOCOL_VERSION, CLIENT_LIMIT_MESSAGE, DirectoryMachine, ConnectPlan, RelayStatus, IceServer, SignalData from @overdeck/contracts. Fallback: create packages/anywhere-channel/src/directory-frames.ts with a verbatim copy of those client-role types/constants from git show origin/feature/pan-4828:packages/contracts/src/connect.ts, headed '// TEMPORARY copy of PAN-4828 contracts; delete and import from @overdeck/contracts once PAN-4828 merges.' Never merge origin/feature/pan-4828. Implement DirectoryWebClient per the PRD WI-7 API: socket URL wss://<host>/v1/directory from baseUrl (http->ws); new WebSocket(url, ['overdeck.bearer.'+token]); on open require socket.protocol to equal the offered protocol else close and reconnect; send hello-client {type, protocol, clientId, label (control chars dropped, trimmed, <=64, never empty -> first 8 chars of clientId), publicKeyHex, appVersion (<=32), platform}; pong text updates last pong; welcome-client -> online, reset back-off, store plan/relayAllowed/machines; directory -> machines; error client_limit -> refusal; deliver frames to on() handlers (a throwing handler does not stop others); ping every 30 s, drop+reconnect after 75 s without pong; closes 4001/4003/4010/4011/4012/4013 -> refused (no retry; 4013 -> CLIENT_LIMIT_MESSAGE); other closes -> back-off 1000 ms doubling to 300000 ms times (1 + (random()*2-1)*0.2); send() false unless online; iceServers(relay) sends ice-servers with a 32-hex requestId and resolves on the matching reply, rejects on a matching error or after 10000 ms; a null token opens no socket. Tests inject a fake WebSocket class and random: () => 0.5, use vi.useFakeTimers(). Do not edit web.ts (dial-machine adds the export).

items.title: Given a token odd_<64 hex>, when start() runs, then the fake WebSocket is constructed with protocol overdeck.bearer.<token> and, after open, receives a hello-client frame carrying clientId, label, publicKeyHex, appVersion, platform and protocol 1
Given repeated close code 1006, the client reconnects after 1000, 2000 and 4000 ms and never waits longer than 300000 ms
Given close code 4013, the client sets state refused with CLIENT_LIMIT_MESSAGE and opens no new socket after advancing 600000 ms
Given 75 s without a pong, the client drops the socket and opens a new one; given a welcome-client frame, state becomes online and machines equals the frame's list
iceServers(true) resolves with the reply whose requestId matches and rejects after 10000 ms without one
Add RtcDuplexWeb: a streamx Duplex over a browser RTCDataChannel with the server's limits

narrative.Action: PRD WI-8. export class RtcDuplexWeb extends streamx Duplex with RTC_MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES=16*1024, RTC_HIGH_WATER_BYTES=1024*1024, RTC_LOW_WATER_BYTES=256*1024 (same names/values as src/lib/anywhere/channel/rtc-duplex.ts). Constructor (channel: RTCDataChannel, peerId): binaryType='arraybuffer', bufferedAmountLowThreshold=RTC_LOW_WATER_BYTES, remoteAddress='rtc:'+peerId.replace(/-/g,'').slice(0,16); message events push new Uint8Array(data) (strings via b4a.from(data,'utf8')) and count bytesIn; close event pushes null and destroys. _write(data, cb): error when channel not open; send slices <=16 KiB; count bytesOut; cb() at once when bufferedAmount <= 1 MiB else on next bufferedamountlow event. _final/_destroy close the channel unless closing/closed. _read(cb) calls cb(). Tests use a FakeDataChannel extends EventTarget with settable readyState/bufferedAmount recording send calls. Do not edit web.ts (dial-machine adds the export).

items.title: When 40 KiB is written, then the fake channel receives sends of 16384, 16384 and 8192 bytes in order
Given bufferedAmount of 2 MiB, the write callback stays pending until a bufferedamountlow event is dispatched, then completes
When a message event carrying an ArrayBuffer is dispatched, the duplex emits identical bytes on its readable side
A close event emits end and close on the duplex, destroy() calls channel.close() exactly once, and a write after close fails with an error
Add createMachineDialer/dialMachine: WebRTC dial to a machine through directory signal frames, one peer connection per machine

metadata.parallelSafeReason: Owns its new files; its only shared file, web.ts, is serialized behind web-secure-channel by an edge.

narrative.Action: PRD WI-9, decision D-8 (the machine's RtcTransport.accept closes an older peer connection for the same (from, relay, purpose) key, so the phone must reuse one RTCPeerConnection per machine). createMachineDialer(directory: Pick<DirectoryWebClient,'send'|'on'|'iceServers'>, deps?: { RTCPeerConnection? }) returns { dialMachine(environmentId, { relay, signal?, timeoutMs? = 15000 }): Promise<RtcDuplexWeb>; close(environmentId?) }. Cache key '<environmentId>|relay' or '|direct'; reuse unless connectionState failed/closed/disconnected; concurrent first dials share one creation promise. Create: iceServers = await directory.iceServers(relay); new RTCPeerConnection({ iceServers, iceTransportPolicy: relay ? 'relay' : 'all' }); session = 32 lowercase hex; first createDataChannel('ovdl', { ordered: true }) BEFORE createOffer; setLocalDescription; send { type:'signal', to: environmentId, session, purpose:'link', relay, data:{ sdp:{ type:'offer', sdp } } }; local candidates gathered before the offer are queued then flushed as { candidate:{ candidate, sdpMid: sdpMid ?? null, sdpMLineIndex: sdpMLineIndex ?? null } }. Ignore signal frames unless session and from match; first answer sets remote description and flushes queued remote candidates; addIceCandidate errors swallowed. An error frame with this session closes the entry and rejects pending dials with Error(frame.message). Later dials open another ovdl channel on the live pc. Resolve new RtcDuplexWeb(channel, environmentId) on open; reject on close-before-open, connectionState failed/closed, abort (Error name AbortError) or timeout; close the entry only if no channel ever opened on it. pc.ondatachannel channels are closed at once. web.ts: export RtcDuplexWeb and its three constants, DirectoryWebClient and its types, createMachineDialer, type MachineDialer, type ClientSignaling. Tests inject FakePeerConnection/FakeDataChannel and a fake directory; vi.useFakeTimers().

items.title: Given a first dial with relay true, then exactly one signal frame with purpose link, a 32-hex session and an offer sdp is sent, and the peer connection was constructed with iceTransportPolicy relay
The dialer sends candidates gathered before the offer only after the offer frame, and it ignores an answer whose from differs from the machine id (no setRemoteDescription call is recorded)
Two dials to the same machine create one peer connection and two ovdl data channels; a dial after the connection reports failed creates a new peer connection
An error frame carrying the dial's session rejects the pending dial with its message, and a dial with no answer rejects after advancing 15000 ms
web.ts exports openSecureChannel, RtcDuplexWeb, DirectoryWebClient and createMachineDialer

metadata.parallelSafeReason: Creates only new files under packages/anywhere-channel/cp1 and tests/integration/anywhere; nothing else edits them.

narrative.Action: PRD WI-10, decisions D-11 and D-12 (pan-4823 CP-1, AC-5 second half). cp1/vite.config.ts: root cp1/, outDir cp1/dist (ignored by the existing .gitignore 'dist/' rule), target es2020, resolve.alias { events: 'bare-events', 'sodium-native': 'sodium-javascript' }. cp1/ws-duplex.ts: streamx Duplex over a browser WebSocket (binaryType arraybuffer). cp1/harness.ts: read ws and code from location.search; key pair from noise-handshake/dh generateKeyPair(); time openSecureChannel(pairing) as handshakeMs; write 64 x 16 KiB; wait for the responder's 4-byte 'done'; transferMs; report {engine: navigator.userAgent, ok, handshakeMs, transferMs, error?} by POST /result and in <pre id=result>. cp1/serve.ts exports startCp1Server({host, port}) -> { url, pairingCode, results, close() }: serves cp1/dist, accepts /channel WebSockets (ws WebSocketServer + createWebSocketStream) into acceptChannel (src/lib/anywhere/channel/accept.ts) with a fresh key and takePairing matching pairingSecrets(nodeCrypto, pairingCode); writes 'done' at 1048576 bytes; when run directly (npx tsx packages/anywhere-channel/cp1/serve.ts --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8791) it builds with Vite's build() API, prints the URL and each result, exits after the first result or 10 minutes. cp1-browsers.slow.test.ts builds, starts the server on 127.0.0.1:0, runs Playwright chromium (CDP Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate {rate: 4} before navigating) and webkit, waits for #result (60 s ceiling), asserts ok. Android leg: ~/Android/Sdk/emulator/emulator -avd galaxyA16 -no-window -no-audio -no-snapshot-save in background; adb wait-for-device; wait for sys.boot_completed=1; start serve.ts on 0.0.0.0:8791; adb shell am start -a android.intent.action.VIEW -d 'http://10.0.2.2:8791/?ws=ws://10.0.2.2:8791/channel&code=<code>'; record result; adb emu kill. Fallbacks (D-12): no browser on the AVD or no boot within 5 min -> record 'Android leg not run: <reason>' and apply the 2 s bar to throttled Chromium; iOS Simulator leg is not run here -> record 'iOS Simulator leg deferred to PAN-4837 (W-APP1); Playwright WebKit stands in'; WebKit launch failure -> record the error, leg not run. Pass bar: handshake ok in every leg run and 1 MiB < 2 s on the Android emulator (or throttled Chromium under fallback). Only if the bar fails: implement the libsodium-wrappers adapter per PRD WI-10 step 7 in packages/anywhere-channel/src/sodium-wasm.ts, re-run, record both; if that also fails, pan tell flywheel-orchestrator and stop. CP-1.md records date, commit, engine/user agent, handshakeMs, transferMs, pass/fail per leg.
